reason: Capsules can be suberect, which is an orientation of the whole fruit.
A bracteole can be large or enlarged.

Antrorse describes the direction of hairs, prickles or teeth, not the lamina itself. A rule would need to attach it to the hair or margin tooth. It is acceptable only when the examples are about the lamina surface.
Stems can be ciliate. Some examples describe margins of parts on the stem, but the pair is meaningful.
Roots and taproots can be straight.
Ligulate or strap-shaped lobes are a normal lobe shape.
Examples such as 'foot 3 mm long' are a measured length of the part.
'Long-stalked' describes the stalk of the sporangium, not the length of the sporangium. This is a wrong reading, so the stalk should carry the length.
Small lobes and small lips are meaningful.
Embryo colour (white, green, yellow-brown) is a normal character.
The colour of bases and sheaths is meaningful.
Mericarps can be wrinkled.
Leaf veins can be pubescent or glabrous, so hairiness applies.
Veins are vascular bundles, and sinuous or tortuous veins are a real character. The examples mean veins, not bundles of the stem.
Inrolled leaf margins are a standard character, and introverted fits that meaning.
Sori can be curved.
Hypanthium thickness is measured, for example in fruit.
Disk glands can have a truncate apex.
Size of pinnules and blades, and subequal size, are meaningful.
Persistent stipes, meaning not shed, are meaningful.
'Base oblique' means an asymmetric base shape, not an orientation. A rule would need to map oblique base or shape to a shape term and keep orientation for angled parts.
The examples are about a midrib and rhizome scales, not trichomes. The part is wrong, so the pair comes from a wrong reading.
Epicalyx bracts have a shape.
Disk glands can be fleshy.
Bracts can be woody, and ligneous is the same thing.
Free versus connate lobes is a meaningful attachment character.
Peristome teeth can be filiform.
Thick or thickened walls are meaningful.
Rachis internodes can be ciliate.
'Obliquely elliptic' and 'base oblique' mean an asymmetric shape, not orientation. A rule would need to separate shape or asymmetry from orientation.
A disc can be grooved.
Capitula can be clustered.
A rostellum or lobe can be broad.
Cladodes can be grooved.
An ovary can be large or enlarged, for example in fruit.
Pinnae and pinnules can be ascending.
'Delicate' here means slender or thin, not breakable. Fragile is the wrong reading, and a slenderness term should be used instead.
Internodes can be hollow or fistulose.
Anthers can be penicillate, with a tuft of hairs at the apex.
Legumes have an outline shape, such as oblong or elliptic.
Lateral veins can be patent or spreading.
Shoots and stems can be terete.
Lobes can be semicircular or semiorbicular.
Pseudobulbs can be subcylindric.
'Acute' as an apex shape is not physical sharpness. A rule would need to map acute apex or tip shapes to a shape term.
Equal and unequal size of paired parts such as pollinia is meaningful.
Anthers can be pendent.
The inner surface of a sepal can be sericeous.
Ovaries can be hemispherical.
'Compressed' means flattened, not condensed. PATO_0001485 means something else, so this is a wrong reading.
A spike can be long.
Disk and lobe outlines are shapes.
Lobes can be obovate.
Examples mix keel, crest and ridge, and 'à pièces entières' means undivided. A rule would need to say whether this is an entire margin or an undivided part.
Cupules can be solitary.
Sepals can be floccose.
Internodes can be clavate.
A disk or lobe can be smooth.
An ovary can be dilated.
A septum can be membranous, which is a texture.
